tool.name: query_metrics
tool.title: Query Analytics Metrics
tool.description:
Query analytics metrics for this company over a date range. Returns aggregate totals and, if groupByTime or groupByDimensions is set, all grouped rows (the server paginates metricsTable in pages of 1000 edges until complete; paginationPagesFetched reports how many GraphQL calls were used). Use list_metrics first to discover valid metric IDs; when batching multiple metrics with groupByTime, every metric must support that granularity on the date dimension (call list_metrics with metricIds to get commonDateGranularities).

IMPORTANT: Some metrics (e.g. creative_impressions_v2, _v2 metrics) require a dimension grouping to return non-null aggregates — add groupByDimensions: ["creative_id"] if aggregates are null. Check aggregateErrors in the response to understand why any metric returned null.

endDate.description: End date in YYYY-MM-DD format. Defaults to today.

dimension.description: Dimension ID to filter on (e.g. "channel", "creative_id"). Must be a dimension supported by the requested metrics — use list_metrics to check.

filters.description: Optional dimension filters. The date range is always applied automatically.

metricIds.description: One or more metric IDs to query. Use list_metrics to discover valid IDs (e.g. "campaign_revenue_aggregate_group").

groupByTime.description: Time granularity for grouping rows. Omit to return only aggregate totals with no time breakdown. Must be listed on the date dimension for every metric in metricIds (intersection); use list_metrics with the same metricIds to read commonDateGranularities.

userRequestId.description: Optional universal MCP-server telemetry only. Generate a UUID4 and reuse the same UUID4 for all tool calls caused by the same human request.

groupByDimensions.description: Additional dimensions to group rows by (e.g. "creative_id", "campaign"). Some metrics — particularly creative_impressions_v2 and other _v2 metrics — require at least one dimension grouping to return non-null aggregates. Use list_metrics to see which dimensions each metric supports.
